column1: 1:1|Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, to the saints who are [in Ephesus] and faithful in Christ Jesus:|Retains the bracketed place-name uncertainty in the pinned Greek.
1:2|Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.|Keeps the paired greeting and both sources.
1:3|Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly realms.|Preserves repeated blessing and heavenly location.
1:4|For he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.|Keeps divine choice, time, purpose, and love's possible attachment.
1:5|He predestined us for adoption as sons through Jesus Christ to himself, according to the good pleasure of his will,|Preserves divine purpose and gendered inheritance status.
1:6|to the praise of his glorious grace, which he freely bestowed on us in the Beloved.|Keeps praise, grace wordplay, and Christ's title.
1:7|In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of trespasses, according to the wealth of his grace|Preserves costly release, forgiveness, and abundance.
1:8|that he lavished on us, with all wisdom and understanding.|Keeps overflowing grace and its manner/context.
1:9|He made known to us the mystery of his will, according to his good pleasure that he purposed in Christ,|Preserves revealed purpose and mystery language.

1:10|for an administration at the fullness of the times: to bring together all things in Christ, things in the heavens and things on earth—in him.|Keeps timing, administrative image, and cosmic scope.

1:11|In him we also received an inheritance, having been predestined according to the purpose of the one who works all things according to the counsel of his will,|Preserves inheritance/passive-lot range and comprehensive purpose.
1:12|so that we, who were the first to hope in Christ, might live for the praise of his glory.|Keeps temporal priority and purpose.

1:13|In him you also, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation, and believed in him, were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit.|Preserves hearing, believing, sealing, and the Spirit's title.
1:14|The Spirit is the down payment of our inheritance until the redemption of God's possession, to the praise of his glory.|Keeps pledge, inheritance, possession, and praise.
1:15|For this reason, because I have heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,|Preserves report, faith, and variant-marked love.
1:16|I do not stop giving thanks for you as I remember you in my prayers.|Keeps continual thanksgiving and remembrance.
1:17|I pray that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you a spirit of wisdom and revelation in knowing him.|Preserves divine titles and requested knowledge.

1:18|May the eyes of your heart be enlightened so that you may know the hope of his calling, the wealth of his glorious inheritance among the saints,|Keeps bodily metaphor, hope, wealth, and communal setting.
1:19|and the surpassing greatness of his power toward us who believe, according to the working of his mighty strength.|Preserves stacked power terms and believing recipients.
1:20|God exercised this power in Christ when he raised him from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly realms,|Keeps resurrection, enthronement, and location.
1:21|far above every ruler, authority, power, and dominion, and every name that is named, not only in this age but also in the age to come.|Preserves complete power list and both ages.
1:22|He subjected everything under Christ's feet and gave him as head over everything to the church,|Keeps subjection, body image, and gift to church.
1:23|which is his body, the fullness of the one who fills all things in every way.|Preserves dense fullness/filling wordplay.
2:1|And you were dead in your trespasses and sins,|Keeps the unfinished opening and death metaphor.

2:2|in which you once walked according to the age of this world, according to the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit now working in the children of disobedience.|Preserves former walk, cosmic ruler, air, and active spirit.

2:3|All of us also once lived among them in the desires of our flesh, doing what the flesh and our thoughts willed, and we were by nature children of wrath like the rest.|Keeps inclusive confession, desires, mind, and wrath idiom.
2:4|But God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us,|Preserves divine contrast and love repetition.
2:5|even when we were dead in trespasses, made us alive together with Christ—by grace you have been saved—|Keeps co-life, interruption, and completed salvation.
2:6|and raised us together and seated us together in the heavenly realms in Christ Jesus,|Preserves both co- verbs and location.
2:7|so that in the coming ages he might demonstrate the surpassing wealth of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus.|Keeps future display, abundance, and kindness.
2:8|For by grace you have been saved through faith, and this is not from yourselves; it is God's gift,|Preserves grace, faith, denial of self-source, and gift.
2:9|not from works, so that no one may boast.|Keeps the concise exclusion and purpose.
2:10|For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand so that we would walk in them.|Preserves creation, prepared works, and walking image.

2:11|Therefore remember that formerly you, Gentiles in the flesh—called “uncircumcision” by what is called “circumcision,” performed in the flesh by human hands—|Keeps ethnic/bodily labels and their human construction.

2:12|remember that at that time you were without Christ, alienated from the citizenship of Israel and strangers to the covenants of promise, having no hope and without God in the world.|Preserves the full fivefold estrangement.
2:13|But now in Christ Jesus, you who once were far away have been brought near by Christ's blood.|Keeps spatial reversal and costly means.
2:14|For he himself is our peace. He made the two one and in his flesh tore down the dividing wall, the hostility.|Preserves Christ as peace, two-to-one, wall, body, and hostility.
2:15|He nullified the law of commandments in decrees so that in himself he might create the two into one new humanity, making peace,|Keeps legal action, creation, two-to-one, and peace.
2:16|and reconcile both to God in one body through the cross, killing the hostility through it.|Preserves both groups, body, cross, and violent end of hostility.
2:17|He came and proclaimed peace to you who were far away and peace to those who were near,|Keeps repeated peace and distance groups.
2:18|because through him both groups have access in one Spirit to the Father.|Preserves mediation, both, unity, and destination.
2:19|So then, you are no longer strangers and resident foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of God's household.|Keeps political and household status reversal.
2:20|You have been built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the cornerstone.|Preserves construction and foundation roles.
2:21|In him the whole building, joined together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord.|Keeps organic growth and temple image.
2:22|And in him you also are being built together into a dwelling place for God in the Spirit.|Preserves ongoing communal construction and divine dwelling.
3:1|For this reason I, Paul, the prisoner of Christ Jesus for the sake of you Gentiles—|Keeps interrupted sentence and Paul's re-description of imprisonment.
3:2|surely you have heard about the stewardship of God's grace that was given to me for you,|Preserves conditional tone, entrusted administration, and recipients.
3:3|that by revelation the mystery was made known to me, as I wrote briefly before.|Keeps revelation, mystery, and prior writing.
3:4|When you read this, you can understand my insight into the mystery of Christ,|Preserves reader access and object of insight.
3:5|which was not made known to people in other generations as it has now been revealed by the Spirit to his holy apostles and prophets:|Keeps comparison across generations and present revelation.
3:6|the Gentiles are coheirs, members of the same body, and copartners in the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.|Preserves three co- compounds and equal participation.
3:7|I became a servant of this gospel according to the gift of God's grace given to me through the working of his power.|Keeps service, gift, grace, and power.
3:8|This grace was given to me, the very least of all the saints: to proclaim to the Gentiles the unsearchable wealth of Christ|Preserves Paul's intensified self-description and mission.
3:9|and to bring to light for everyone the administration of the mystery hidden for ages in God, who created all things.|Keeps universal disclosure, hidden duration, and Creator.

3:10|This was so that now, through the church, God's richly varied wisdom might be made known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly realms,|Preserves church as means, multicolored image, and heavenly powers.
3:11|according to the eternal purpose he accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord.|Keeps purpose's duration and accomplishment.
3:12|In him we have boldness and confident access through his faithfulness.|Renders the genitive as Christ's faithfulness and preserves access.
3:13|Therefore I ask you not to lose heart because of my afflictions for you, which are your glory.|Names affliction and Paul's surprising evaluation.
3:14|For this reason I bend my knees before the Father,|Keeps bodily prayer posture and resumed phrase.
3:15|from whom every family in heaven and on earth receives its name.|Preserves Father/family wordplay and total scope.
3:16|I pray that, according to the wealth of his glory, he may grant you to be strengthened with power through his Spirit in your inner being,|Keeps prayer, wealth, Spirit, and inner person.
3:17|so that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are rooted and grounded in love.|Preserves dwelling plus agricultural and construction metaphors.
3:18|May you have strength to grasp, together with all the saints, what is the width and length and height and depth,|Keeps four dimensions without supplying an unstated object.
3:19|and to know Christ's love that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled to all the fullness of God.|Preserves knowledge paradox and fullness.
3:20|Now to the one who is able to do far beyond all that we ask or imagine, according to the power at work within us,|Keeps extraordinary abundance and active power.
3:21|to him be glory in the church and in Christ Jesus through all generations, forever and ever. Amen.|Preserves both locations of glory and expansive duration.
4:1|Therefore I, the prisoner in the Lord, urge you to walk in a manner worthy of the calling with which you were called,|Keeps prisoner identity, exhortation, and calling repetition.
4:2|with all humility and gentleness, with patience, bearing with one another in love,|Preserves the four relational qualities.
4:3|making every effort to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace:|Keeps Spirit as unity's source and peace as bond.
4:4|one body and one Spirit, just as you were also called in one hope of your calling;|Preserves repeated one and calling.
4:5|one Lord, one faith, one baptism;|Keeps the terse threefold confession.
4:6|one God and Father of all, who is over all, through all, and in all.|Preserves repeated all and three relations.
4:7|But grace was given to each one of us according to the measure of Christ's gift.|Keeps movement from unity to individual gift and measured grace.
4:8|Therefore it says, “When he ascended on high, he took captivity captive; he gave gifts to people.”|Retains unusual captive-captivity wording and gift shift.
4:9|Now what does “he ascended” mean except that he also descended into the lower parts of the earth?|Keeps interpretive question and geographic ambiguity.
4:10|The one who descended is also the one who ascended far above all the heavens, so that he might fill all things.|Preserves same subject, movement, and purpose.
4:11|And he himself gave some as apostles, some as prophets, some as evangelists, and some as pastors and teachers,|Keeps persons as gifts and the five designations.
4:12|to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up Christ's body,|Preserves equipping, saints' ministry, and bodily construction.
4:13|until all of us reach unity in the faith and in knowing the Son of God, mature humanity, the measure of the stature of Christ's fullness.|Keeps communal goal and adult/fullness measure.

4:14|Then we will no longer be children, tossed by waves and carried around by every wind of teaching, by human trickery and cunning schemes that lead into error.|Preserves sea/weather images and intentional deception.
4:15|Instead, speaking truth in love, let us grow in every way into him who is the head—Christ.|Keeps truth-as-action, love, growth, and head image.

4:16|From him the whole body, joined and held together by every supporting ligament, grows and builds itself up in love as each individual part does its work in proper measure.|Preserves integrated body and each part's measured action.
4:17|Therefore I say this and testify in the Lord: you must no longer walk as the Gentiles also walk, in the futility of their minds.|Keeps solemn charge and walk/mind relation.

4:18|They are darkened in understanding and alienated from God's life because of the ignorance within them, because of the hardness of their hearts.|Preserves mental, relational, causal, and bodily imagery.
4:19|Having become callous, they gave themselves over to debauchery, to practice every kind of impurity with greed.|Keeps self-surrender, practice, and acquisitive excess.
4:20|But that is not how you learned Christ,|Retains Christ as the person learned and the interrupted thought.
4:21|if indeed you heard him and were taught in him, just as truth is in Jesus:|Keeps conditional force, direct hearing, and truth relation.

4:22|you were taught to put off the old person belonging to your former way of life, which is being corrupted by deceitful desires,|Preserves clothing metaphor, former conduct, and continuing corruption.
4:23|to be renewed in the spirit of your minds,|Keeps passive renewal and mental sphere.
4:24|and to put on the new person, created according to God in the righteousness and holiness that come from truth.|Preserves clothing, creation, divine pattern, and truth.
4:25|Therefore, putting away falsehood, “each of you speak truth with your neighbor,” because we are members of one another.|Keeps quotation and bodily reason for truthfulness.
4:26|“Be angry, but do not sin.” Do not let the sun set while you remain provoked,|Preserves command, limit, sun image, and ongoing irritation.
4:27|and do not give the devil an opportunity.|Keeps the spatial opportunity metaphor.

4:28|The one who steals must steal no longer, but rather must labor, doing good work with their own hands, so that they may have something to share with anyone in need.|Preserves cessation, work, bodily means, and generosity's purpose.

4:29|Let no rotten word come out of your mouth, but only what is good for building up as the need requires, so that it may give grace to those who hear.|Keeps decay image, situational benefit, and grace.
4:30|And do not grieve God's Holy Spirit, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.|Preserves personal grief, seal, and future day.
4:31|Let all bitterness, rage, anger, shouting, and slander be removed from you, along with every kind of malice.|Keeps the complete harmful-speech/anger list.
4:32|Instead, be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving each other just as God in Christ forgave you.|Preserves mutuality and divine pattern.
5:1|Therefore imitate God, as dearly loved children,|Keeps divine imitation grounded in beloved kinship.
5:2|and walk in love, just as Christ loved us and gave himself for us as an offering and sacrifice to God, a fragrant aroma.|Preserves self-giving, cultic terms, and fragrance image.
5:3|But sexual immorality, every kind of impurity, or greed must not even be named among you, as is fitting for saints.|Keeps broad categories and community standard.
5:4|Nor should there be shameful behavior, foolish talk, or crude joking, which are improper, but rather thanksgiving.|Preserves speech contrasts and thanksgiving wordplay.

5:5|For know this with certainty: no sexually immoral, impure, or greedy person—who is an idolater—has an inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.|Keeps vice identities, greed/idolatry relation, and inheritance.
5:6|Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things God's wrath comes upon the children of disobedience.|Preserves warning, cause, wrath, and kinship idiom.
5:7|Therefore do not become partners with them.|Keeps partnership prohibition concise.
5:8|For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Walk as children of light—|Preserves identity contrast and movement command.
5:9|for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness, and truth—|Keeps light-fruit metaphor and three qualities.
5:10|testing what is pleasing to the Lord.|Preserves active discernment linked to walking.
5:11|Do not participate in the fruitless works of darkness, but instead expose them.|Keeps participation/exposure contrast.
5:12|For it is shameful even to speak of the things they do in secret.|Preserves secrecy and speech restraint.
5:13|But everything exposed by the light becomes visible,|Keeps exposure and manifestation.
5:14|for everything made visible is light. Therefore it says, “Wake up, sleeper, and rise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”|Preserves difficult light claim and poetic summons.
5:15|Therefore watch carefully how you walk—not as unwise people but as wise,|Keeps exact attention, movement image, and contrast.
5:16|buying up the opportunity, because the days are evil.|Retains commercial time image and moral reason.
5:17|Because of this, do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord's will is.|Keeps wisdom contrast and object.
5:18|Do not get drunk with wine, which leads to reckless living, but be filled by the Spirit,|Preserves intoxication/consequence and Spirit contrast.
5:19|speaking to one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making melody to the Lord with your heart,|Keeps mutual speech, three song forms, and inward music.
5:20|always giving thanks for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,|Preserves both comprehensive terms and divine relations.
5:21|submitting to one another in reverence for Christ.|Keeps mutual submission as the participial frame.
5:22|Wives, submit to your own husbands as to the Lord,|Supplies the verb from the immediately preceding mutual-submission clause.
5:23|because a husband is head of his wife as Christ is head of the church, he himself the Savior of the body.|Preserves husband/wife specificity and head/body comparison.
5:24|But as the church submits to Christ, so wives should submit to their husbands in everything.|Keeps the comparison and comprehensive wording.
5:25|Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself for her,|Preserves direct gendered command and self-giving standard.
5:26|so that he might make her holy, cleansing her by the washing of water with the word,|Keeps sanctifying purpose, feminine church, washing, and word.
5:27|so that he might present the church to himself in splendor, without spot or wrinkle or anything like that, but holy and blameless.|Preserves presentation, bodily images, and ethical purpose.
5:28|In the same way, husbands ought to love their own wives as their own bodies. The man who loves his own wife loves himself,|Keeps bodily identity and male specificity.
5:29|for no one ever hated his own flesh, but nourishes and tenderly cares for it, just as Christ does the church,|Preserves nourishment and tender bodily care.
5:30|because we are members of his body.|Keeps corporate bodily relation.
5:31|“For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.”|Preserves gender, movement, union, and quotation.
5:32|This mystery is great, and I am speaking about Christ and the church.|Keeps magnitude and stated referent.
5:33|Nevertheless, each one of you must love his own wife as himself, and the wife should respect her husband.|Preserves differentiated closing commands; respect renders relational fear.
